guide.immersive_smithing.getting_started:
## Your first workshop
Start with stone tongs, a stone hammer, a forge, an anvil and a water trough. Most metal equipment is made here instead of at a crafting table.

## 1. Melt and forge
Add metal to the forge's top and fuel to its bottom. Ignite the fuel. When the metal melts, use empty tongs, choose an item and complete the timing game.

## 2. Shape
Place the workpiece on the anvil with your tongs. Use a hammer and click each target as its ring closes.

## 3. Quench
Pick up the shaped workpiece with empty tongs. Use it on a water-filled trough to receive your finished item.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_forge.te:
## Load the upper half
Right-click with metal to add one item. Sneak-use to add the whole stack. Ingots, nuggets, raw metal, storage blocks and recognised old equipment can be melted.

## Use one metal family
Keep each forge to one family, such as iron or copper. Add fuel to the lower half, ignite it, and wait for the metal to melt.

## Taking metal back
While the forge is not heating, sneak-use its top with an empty hand to remove the last unmelted deposit.

Molten metal must be forged into an item. A forge containing molten metal cannot be broken in survival. A comparator reads 15 when it is ready.
guide.immersive_smithing.fuels_and_ignit:
## Solid fuel
Right-click the lower half with fuel: logs, planks, wooden slabs, sticks, coal, charcoal or coal blocks. Then ignite it with Flint and Steel or a Fire Charge. The fire only burns while there is metal to melt.

## Lava
Lava is different: pour a lava bucket into the lower half and it heats the forge straight away, with no ignition. An empty bucket scoops a full bucket back out.

## Recover unused fuel
Sneak-use with an empty hand on the lower half to take back fuel that is not burning.
guide.immersive_smithing.material_famili:
## One family per forge
Every metal belongs to a material family: iron, gold, copper, netherite, and metals from other mods found through their forge:ingots tags.

## Material units
Items are worth material units: a nugget is 1, an ingot or raw ore is 9 and a storage block is 81. Each item costs units, so an iron sword needs 18 (two ingots) plus a stick.

## Melting speed
Families melt at different speeds. Gold melts quickly, netherite slowly.
## Choose an item
Use empty tongs on a forge with molten metal. Search or browse the available recipes. Only recipes you can afford in metal and components appear.

## Time each press
Press Space or left-click as the marker crosses the glowing zone. Aim for the bright centre. Each pass takes one press; waiting makes the marker faster.

## What your score means
Accurate timing improves durability. If time runs out, you still receive a workpiece, with a Forge score of 0.

## Cancel safely
Close the screen to cancel without using metal. Components reserved from your inventory, such as sticks, are returned.
## Carry hot metal
Tongs start forging and carry hot workpieces. Every use is a quick stab: into the forge, onto the anvil, into the trough. A workpiece stays in the tongs until you set it down; it cannot be equipped and it never cools.

## Dropped tongs
If you drop the tongs or die, the workpiece stays in them, and anyone can pick them up and carry on.

## Recycle a workpiece
Sneak-use loaded tongs on a forge to melt the workpiece back into metal; its components are lost. Tongs wear by one for each forging and one for each quench.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_anvil.te:
## Place and retrieve
Use loaded tongs on the anvil to set the workpiece down, and empty tongs to pick it up again. The anvil holds one workpiece. While someone is working at it, nobody else can take or start the workpiece.

## If the anvil breaks
If an anvil is broken, its workpiece drops as a Hot Workpiece item. Use empty tongs in the air to pick it up, or right-click an anvil with it.

## Repairs and names
The Smith's Anvil does not repair or rename items; that is still the vanilla anvil's job.
## Start shaping
Use a Smithing Hammer on an anvil holding a forged workpiece. Targets appear one at a time.

## Aim and time your strike
Click near the target's centre just as the white ring closes onto it. The faint ring previews the next target.

Missed strikes reduce your score. Expired targets return, costing more time.

## Finish every target
Your Anvil score sets efficacy: damage, mining speed or armor points. Running out of time before finishing makes the workpiece Faulty.

Closing the screen or disconnecting cancels safely. You can try again.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_trough.t:
## Fill with water
Use water buckets on the trough. One bucket provides four quenches by default. Pipes can also supply water.

## Finish the item
Hold tongs carrying a shaped workpiece and use them on the trough. Hammer the workpiece at the anvil first; unshaped metal cannot be quenched.

The finished item enters your inventory. If there is no room, it drops at the trough.
guide.immersive_smithing.makers_mark.tex:
## Every piece knows its smith
A quenched item records who forged it: hover over it and it says Crafted by you. The mark stays through repairs, enchanting, dyeing and elemental upgrades; only melting the piece down removes it.

## Title and inscription
Right after the quench a small screen lets you give the piece a title and up to three lines of inscription. Leave it unsigned if you prefer, and sign it later: sneak-use the Smith's Anvil while holding the finished piece. Faulty work cannot be signed.

## Found gear
Equipment from chests and treasure carries an honest grade of its own, never better than Standard, so a Fine or Masterwork piece was always made by a smith.
guide.immersive_smithing.equipment_quali:
## Forge: durability
Smithed items carry two scores. The Forge score sets durability: at 50 an item lasts as long as usual, at 100 it lasts a quarter longer and at 0 a quarter less.

## Anvil: efficacy
The Anvil score sets efficacy: attack damage for weapons, mining speed for tools and armor points for armor. At 50 it is ordinary; at 100 it is fifteen percent better.

The overall label averages both scores: Crude (below 35), Standard (35 to 69), Fine (70 to 89) and Masterwork (90 and above). Hold Shift over an item for details. Equipment without smithing data, such as loot, behaves exactly like Standard.
guide.immersive_smithing.faulty_equipmen:
## What Faulty means
A workpiece whose Anvil timer ran out is Faulty. Faulty items work, but poorly: by default they have half the durability and seventy percent of the efficacy.

## How to recover
The Smith's Grindstone cannot fix them. Melt them down and forge again instead; you keep all of the metal.
guide.immersive_smithing.reforging.title: Reforging
guide.immersive_smithing.reforging.text:
## Recover the metal
Metal equipment the forge recognises can go back into a forge of its family: enchanted, Faulty or anything in between. By default all of its metal is recovered.

## What is lost
Enchantments, quality, custom names and repair history are lost when it melts. Datapacks can mark special items as not recyclable.
guide.immersive_smithing.smiths_grindsto:
## Choose a quality
Hold a smithed item. Use the grindstone to improve durability, or sneak-use to improve efficacy.

## Review and confirm
The first use shows the experience-level cost. Use it again within three seconds to pay and refine.

## Refinement limits
Each refinement adds 5 points, up to 100. Higher scores cost more levels. Enchantments are kept. Faulty items must be melted and forged again.
guide.immersive_smithing.tool_tiers.text:
## Time and durability
Tongs and hammers come in stone, iron, diamond and netherite. Higher tiers give more time in the minigames (30, 35, 40 and 45 seconds by default) and last longer.

## Skill still matters
They never add quality on their own: a skilled smith can make Masterwork equipment with stone tools. Repair them with their material at an anvil. Unbreaking and Mending work on them.
guide.immersive_smithing.netherite.title: Netherite
guide.immersive_smithing.netherite.text:
## Forge directly
Netherite equipment is forged directly from netherite ingots; no smithing template or diamond equipment is needed. A netherite sword costs 18 netherite units (two ingots) and a stick.

## Modded upgrades
The same goes for other mods' smithing-table upgrades, such as netherite shields and weapons: they are forged from the metal, in the shape of the item they used to upgrade, and the smithing-table recipe is disabled.

## Lava required
Netherite only melts with lava as the heat source, so pour a lava bucket into the forge. Lava needs no ignition.
guide.immersive_smithing.modded_equipmen:
## Finding modded metals
Immersive Smithing finds metals from other mods through their forge:ingots, nuggets, storage_blocks and raw_materials tags, and studies the crafting recipes of weapons, tools, armor and metal shields.

## Recipe detection
When a recipe uses exactly one metal plus other components such as sticks or leather, it becomes a smithing recipe and the crafting recipe is disabled. A metal shield built on a wooden base shield only needs the metal: the base is not required. Recipes that mix two metals, or are otherwise unclear, are skipped and still crafted normally. Datapacks can add or override anything.

## Spartan Weaponry
Spartan Weaponry is supported out of the box: every metal weapon, including throwing weapons, longbows and heavy crossbows, has its own recipe and anvil pattern. The studded club and cestus need only their iron. Arrows and bolts are still crafted. A thrown weapon keeps its quality in flight, and arrows share the quality of the bow or crossbow that fires them.
guide.immersive_smithing.automation.text:
## Feed your stations
Hoppers and pipes can feed metal into the top and sides of a forge, fuel into its bottom and back, and water into a trough.

## Work by hand
Automation can never choose a recipe, play a minigame, move a workpiece or quench it: every item is made by a smith. Comparators read the forge and the trough.
guide.immersive_smithing.jei.title: JEI
guide.immersive_smithing.jei.text:
## Browse recipes
With Just Enough Items installed, every smithing recipe, including those detected from other mods, appears in the Smithing category. It shows the metal, the components, the anvil pattern and the Forge, Anvil and Trough steps.

## Replaced recipes
Crafting recipes that smithing replaced are not shown.
guide.immersive_smithing.troubleshooting:
## Forge will not start
The forge will not start forging: make sure the metal has melted (the forge glows and bubbles) and that you hold empty tongs.

## No recipes listed
The item list is empty: you need more metal, or a component such as sticks.

## Netherite will not melt
Netherite will not melt: use lava.

## Missing modded item
A modded item cannot be smithed: an operator can run /immersivesmithing report and /immersivesmithing recipe <item> to see why. After changing the server config, run /reload.
